South Korea – Uzbekistan: Who will win this time?

**South Korea – Uzbekistan: Who will win this time?**

Ahead of the friendly match between the national teams of South Korea and Uzbekistan to be held in 2026, we take a look at the chances of both teams.

Both South Korea and Uzbekistan are thoroughly preparing for the Asian Cup, which starts in January, following their unsuccessful performances in the World Cup held in the summer.

## South Korea

**South Korea has won only once in their last five matches**

After three unanswered goals were scored against Ecuador in the first friendly match following their unsuccessful World Cup campaign, interim head coach Roberto Moreno began to be seen almost as a savior of the nation.

However, the next two matches turned into a cold shower for the team — a heavy 1:4 defeat against Uruguay and a 0:0 draw with Venezuela. Additionally, the national team's central defender and one of its leaders, Kim Min-jae, reacted very emotionally to being substituted in the last match. This may indicate that the Spanish coach's relationship with the team is not very good.

**Two players out, one player returned — the squad situation in the team is unstable**

In the first three matches under Roberto Moreno, South Korea's lineup saw rotation mainly on the left flank of defense, while the midfield line was almost completely changed. A similar approach is expected now as well.

Currently, the South Korean national team is not holding its training camp with its best squad. Central defender Lee Gi-hyuk is participating in the Asian Games with the Olympic national team.

Defensive midfielder Paik Seung-ho suffered an injury and returned to Birmingham without playing a single minute. Also, Midtjylland's central forward Cho Gue-sung has left the national team's disposal.

However, there is also positive news — Porto's defensive midfielder Hwang In-beom has recovered from his injury and already appeared on the pitch in the match against Venezuela.

**South Korea has lost to Uzbekistan only once in history**

South Korea's only defeat against Uzbekistan was recorded in the first match played between these teams in 1994.

Since then, the Koreans have won 11 times and drawn four times in 15 head-to-head encounters.

Furthermore, South Korea has won seven out of eight matches played against Uzbekistan on home soil. However, the last such match took place almost 10 years ago. Since then, Uzbek football has developed significantly.

## Uzbekistan

**The streak of failures is behind — Uzbekistan has won two consecutive matches**

After losing all three matches in their World Cup debut, Uzbekistan is playing its initial preparatory matches ahead of the upcoming Asian Cup with a significantly updated squad.

So far, Fabio Cannavaro's experiments are leaving a positive impression. In home friendly matches, Uzbekistan defeated Iran 3:1 and Syria 4:1.

The goals conceded in both matches were due to own goals. Thus, Uzbekistan put an end to an unpleasant streak of five consecutive defeats against teams representing other continents.

**A number of starting lineup players rested in the match against Syria**

Fabio Cannavaro is testing new options in every line, without calling up a number of players who started in the World Cup to the training camp.

Following the victory over Iran, in the match against Syria ahead of the trip to South Korea, the Italian coach gave a complete rest to a number of players who had justified his trust. Among them are left-back Sherzod Nasrullaev, central midfielder Azizjon Ganiev, winger Dostonbek Khamdamov, and the national team's top scorer Eldor Shomurodov.

Husayin Norchaev, who started the match, added a brace against Syria to his goal scored against Iran. This is a good sign — healthy competition in the central forward position does no harm.

Additionally, the return of the main goalkeeper Abduvohid Nematov, who missed the match against Iran due to injury, should be specially noted.

**Uzbekistan has not been winning away recently**

The "White Wolves'" last victory outside of Uzbekistan dates back to November 2024. At that time, the DPRK national team was defeated 1:0 in Laos.

The last time Uzbekistan caused serious trouble for an opponent away and won was just over two years ago in the capital of Kyrgyzstan, with a 3:2 scoreline.

All seven matches played outside the country in 2025 and 2026 — away or on neutral ground — ended for Uzbekistan with two draws and five consecutive defeats.

## Probable Lineups

**South Korea — 4-4-2:**

Seung-gyu, Tae-seok, Min-jae, Han-beom, Young-woo, Jin-gyu, In-beom, Hee-chan, Kang-in, Hyeon-gyu, Heung-min.

**Uzbekistan — 4-3-3:**

Nematov, Karimov, Khusanov, Urozov, Nasrullaev, Hamrobekov, Ganiev, Mozgovoy, Khamdamov, Fayzullaev, Shomurodov.
